title.t: A buyer's feedback contradicts their stated criteria

when.t: A buyer's reply contains a change-of-mind phrase (for example "forget the", "changed my mind", "matters more"), or an upstream classifier labels it so. Agent 11 marks it and passes it to Agent 13 when the reply names Agent 13 as its owner; rules such as wire or advice come first.
when.src: dispatcher/message_tags.py:33-38, 64-68; dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py::def _route_lead_reply(self, ctx: str, owner, body: dict, env: Envelope | None) -> dict:; dispatcher/listing_spokes_11.py:576

steps.t: Agent 13 asks the buyer, through Agent 11, to confirm the change, quoting their words.

Agent 13 changes nothing: the criteria stay as stated. Only the authorized user changes them, with a signed setting: adding a criterion, or since 2026-10-28 replacing the whole list. The buyer's answer itself is a reply that reaches the authorized user.
The listed phrases are caught, and a label from an upstream classifier is honored too.

never.t: Rewrite the buyer's criteria on its own.

you_see.t: A confirmation request to the buyer.

test.t: Buyer B1's criteria: budget 500,000, 3 bedrooms. B1 writes "Honestly forget the 3 bedrooms, a big yard matters more".

title.t: A criterion points at a protected class

when.t: A signed criterion contains one of these words: "school quality", "school rating", "demographics", "families with", "no children", "race", "religion", "national origin", "ethnic", "families only".

steps.t: Agent 13 refuses that criterion and raises a legal-line alert quoting it; the other criteria are kept.
Only the listed words are caught; a criterion marked as sensitive goes to Compliance instead (13-11).

never.t: Use a criterion that stands in for a protected class.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the criterion.

test.t: Criteria: school rating 9 or higher, 3 bedrooms.

title.t: A listing lacks data on a must-have

when.t: A listing otherwise matches, but has no value for a criterion the buyer marked must-have.

steps.t: Unless the buyer has a standing preference to receive such listings marked unknown, Agent 13 does not send it. It keeps the match, asks the authorized user (naming the missing must-have), and asks the buyer once for that listing whether to send listings like it marked unknown; that question's wording waits for the authorized user's signature, so Agent 11 holds it for now (owner decision of 2026-10-28; before, only the authorized user was asked and the match was dropped).

The buyer's answer is a reply, and it reaches the authorized user. When the authorized user records the buyer's standing preference, the kept matches are checked again and go to the buyer marked unknown.
steps.src: dispatcher/listing_spokes_13.py::if "deliver_unknown_standing_preference" in payload:; dispatcher/listing_spokes_13.py::def _recheck_kept(self, ctx: str, env: Envelope):; dispatcher/listing_spokes_13.py:608-617; tests_listing/test_owner_decisions_2026_10_28.py::def test_missing_must_have_keeps_the_match_and_asks_the_buyer

steps.t: The standing preference, and a replacement of the buyer's whole criteria list, are signed settings; either one checks the kept matches again.

never.t: Send a listing with unknown must-haves as if it matched.

you_see.t: A question naming the missing must-have; the match kept; the question to the buyer held, its wording not yet signed.

test.t: Buyer B1 must have a pool; listing L1 goes live with no pool information.

title.t: A buyer asks "is this a good price?"

when.t: A buyer's reply reaching Agent 13 contains "is this a good price", "good deal", "worth the price" or "should i pay".

steps.t: Agent 13 raises a legal-line alert with the message. Nothing is sent to the buyer.

never.t: Give a view on the price.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the question.

test.t: The buyer writes "Is this a good price for the place on Elm?"

title.t: Too many matches in one day

when.t: A buyer gets more than 5 matches in one day.

steps.t: The first 5 go to the buyer one by one through Agent 11.
The rest wait for the daily run, which sends them as one digest ranked by how many of the buyer's stated criteria each meets.
Every match is logged either way. The digest is ranked only by how many of the buyer's stated criteria each match meets; ties go newest first.
Before any match goes out, Agent 14 must show the buyer agreement on file; without it the matches are held and the authorized user is told once.

never.t: Rank by anything the buyer did not state.

you_see.t: Five match messages and one digest of the sixth.

test.t: Six listings that match buyer B1 go live in one day.

title.t: A buyer's budget and area conflict

when.t: A listing is in the buyer's stated area but priced over the buyer's stated budget.

steps.t: Agent 13 does not send it and asks the authorized user, with the budget and the price.
A listing over budget and outside the area is simply not a match.

never.t: Relax the budget or the area on its own.

you_see.t: A question showing the budget and the price.

test.t: Budget 400,000 in Northside; a Northside listing at 450,000 goes live.

title.t: A match is a colleague's listing

when.t: A matching listing is marked as a colleague's own listing.

steps.t: Agent 13 raises a legal-line alert for the disclosure rules; the match is not sent.
This is a mark on the listing record (colleague_listing); Agent 13 does not work it out.

never.t: Move toward a showing before the disclosure is handled.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert about the colleague's listing.

test.t: A matching listing marked as a colleague's listing goes live.

title.t: A buyer asks what the seller would accept

when.t: A buyer's reply reaching Agent 13 contains "what would the seller take", "seller's bottom line", "what will they accept" or "seller's minimum".

steps.t: Agent 13 raises a legal-line alert with the message. Nothing is sent to the buyer.

never.t: Share anything about the other side's position.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the question.

test.t: The buyer writes "What would the seller take on the Elm Street house?"

title.t: A matching listing has suspect data

when.t: A matching listing is marked with a data anomaly.

steps.t: Agent 13 does not send it and asks the authorized user, quoting the anomaly.
This is a mark on the listing record (data_anomaly); Agent 13 does not work it out.

test.t: A listing marked "sqft 1800 on the sheet, 2400 on the tax record" goes live.

when.t: The authorized user records, as a signed setting, that the buyer's pre-approval expired.

steps.t: Agent 13 sends the buyer a notice through Agent 11.
Matches keep going, each marked as unverified financing.

never.t: Stop the search, or present matches as if financing were verified.

you_see.t: The expiry notice; later matches marked unverified financing.

test.t: The pre-approval is recorded as expired; then a matching listing goes live.

title.t: Compliance does not approve a buyer criterion

when.t: A signed criterion is marked as fair-housing sensitive.

steps.t: Agent 13 sends it to Compliance (Agent 17) and does not use it meanwhile.
If Compliance does not approve it, it is never used for matching, and the authorized user is told which criterion and why.

never.t: Match on a criterion Compliance has not approved.

you_see.t: A question naming the criterion and Compliance's findings.

test.t: Criteria include household "no kids", marked sensitive; Compliance's ruleset prohibits "no kids" (FH-2).
